chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah and others, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said:
If he has intercourse a second time before expiating (the first), then upon him is another expiation; there is no disagreement in this.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if one has intercourse twice before completing the expiation for the first time?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahani's al-Istibsar clarifies the jurisprudence of kaffarah (expiation) for marital intercourse during Ramadan, establishing that each act incurs a distinct obligation if performed before the previous expiation is completed. The phrase 'laysa fi hadhihi khilaf' (there is no difference of opinion) underscores the consensus among Shia jurists on this specific mechanism of cumulative liability, distinguishing it from cases where acts might be merged. This ruling highlights the precision in Shia fiqh regarding the temporal separation of religious duties and their corresponding penalties.
